The map `toCycles i j` regards the coboundary of g as a cocycle, and `iCycles j` forgets that cocycle condition. Their composite is exactly `X.d j i ≫ g`, meaning g composed with the chain differential. This matches [Hatcher §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=206). The reversed indices give the cochain differential its correct direction, with no extra sign. Off-shape differentials are zero; the assertion applies to every coefficient object in the stated abelian k-linear category. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/LinearYoneda.lean#L262).
Published underlying Hom differential fixes the composition and sign.

A coboundary, first viewed as a cocycle by `toCycles`, has zero image under the cohomology quotient `homologyπ`. These are the actual differential factorization and quotient of Hom(X,Y), so the statement expresses that boundaries represent zero, as in [Hatcher §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=206). It makes no assertion that all cocycles are coboundaries. Arbitrary index pairs are valid because off-shape differentials vanish; no representative is chosen from a cohomology class. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/LinearYoneda.lean#L267).
Published formula identifies the represented coboundary as g∘d.

For a chain map f:X′→X, the induced map runs from Hⁱ(Hom(X,Y)) to Hⁱ(Hom(X′,Y)). The equation sends the class of a cocycle to the class of its image under the actual cocycle map, matching the contravariance in [Hatcher §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=209). The adjacent published formula identifies that cocycle map as precomposition with fᵢ. Thus the quotient map has the advertised representatives and direction, without a chosen section or an exactness assumption on Hom. Published underlying cocycle pullback is precomposition by fᵢ.

After forgetting its cocycle condition, the pullback of a cocycle a along f:X′→X is `f.f i ≫ iCycles a`, namely a∘fᵢ. This is the usual cochain pullback of [Hatcher §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=209), with the direction reversed from the chain map. The source proves the equality through naturality of the kernel inclusion and the published component formula. It requires no injectivity of f and makes no identification of cocycles with their cohomology classes. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/LinearYoneda.lean#L283).

This fixes the carrier and degree, rather than merely asserting an unspecified comparison. For contractible X, every singular cycle z in degree q+1 is the boundary of a chain in degree q+2. The source converts the proved vanishing of native positive-degree homology into the elementwise equality ker d=im d. This agrees with homotopy invariance and the point computation in [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=119). The positive-degree restriction is essential and correctly encoded; arbitrary ring coefficients are allowed, and neither a canonical filler nor a bound on its support is claimed. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Contractible.lean#L46).
Published native vanishing theorem specialized in the source proof.

A zero-chain whose coefficient sum is zero is a boundary when X is path connected. The source identifies the native component quotient with the augmentation and uses its proved cokernel property. This is ker ε=im ∂₁ from [Hatcher Proposition 2.7](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=118), with coefficients in any ring. Path connectedness suffices; contractibility is unnecessary. The augmentation hypothesis correctly excludes a nonzero single-point class, and the theorem promises existence of a one-chain rather than a preferred path choice. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Contractible.lean#L88).
Published terminal-minus-initial boundary checks the degree1 convention.
Published augmentation returns the point coefficient.

The augmentation C₍*₎(X;k)→k[0] is a quasi-isomorphism for contractible X: positive homology vanishes, while H₀ maps isomorphically onto k. The proof handles degree zero using ker ε=im ∂₁ and an actual point generator mapping to any coefficient. This is the exact augmented complex from [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=119). Contractibility supplies nonemptiness. The statement correctly retains ordinary H₀ and claims exactness only after augmentation, over an arbitrary ring. This chain isomorphism sends [a⊗c] to a·p₍*₎c for a quotient covering p:E→B. Every base simplex lifts, and any two lifts differ by the G-action; passage to coinvariants removes the choice. The source proves both inverse identities and commutation with the boundary. These are the quotient-chain and diagonal-coinvariant conventions of [Brown §§1,3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=7). Contractibility of E is unnecessary for this chain comparison; it is required separately for the later group-homology interpretation. The forward comparison on the class of a⊗c is exactly a times the pushforward of c to the base. The trivial action on the scalar factor and coinvariant relations make this well defined; no averaging or division by |G| occurs. This matches the diagonal tensor-coinvariant convention in [Brown §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~kbrown/papers/cohomology_hangzhou.pdf#page=13). The formula covers arbitrary chains, coefficients and degrees, and fixes the normalization of the actual chain isomorphism without depending on its chosen simplex-lift inverse. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/GroupHomology.lean#L217).
Published pushforward preserves generator coefficients.

Contractibility makes the identity map homotopic to a constant map through a point. In positive degree, the point has zero singular homology, so the identity on Hₙ(X;R) is zero and the object is zero. The source follows this argument in the stated preadditive category with homology and coproducts, matching [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=119). The hypothesis n≠0 correctly preserves ordinary H₀; no abelian-category or field-coefficient assumption is needed for this argument. Published module-category consequence spells out actual positive-degree filling.

The reduced singular homology object of a contractible space is zero in every nonnegative degree. At zero, reduced homology is the kernel of the augmentation and path connectedness makes that augmentation an isomorphism; in higher degrees the source uses ordinary homology vanishing. This matches the reduced convention of [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=119). `HasKernels` supplies the degree-zero construction. For a chosen point x, this is the canonical isomorphism Hₙ₊₁(X;R)≅Hₙ₊₁(X,{x};R), obtained because the singleton subspace is contractible. For f:X→Y with f(x)=y, pushing an absolute class forward and then passing to homology relative to {y} equals first passing relative to {x} and then applying the induced map of pairs. The displayed map is a bijection between the disjoint union of the summands’ singular n-simplices and the singular n-simplices of their disjoint union.
